statement: SUPPLEMENT to scoring_rule_pattern_skill (registered 2026-10-14), added 2026-10-15 after outside review: the 580 county x measure rows are not independent (a county's errors are correlated across the five measures and across space), so the registered Wilcoxon p-value overstates the evidence. Preferred test: a county-blocked bootstrap of the skill score.
metric: skill = 1 - RMSE_model/RMSE_baseline over all Missouri rows, both relevelled; bootstrap resamples JURISDICTIONS (116 blocks, all five measures per block) with replacement, 10,000 draws
ex_ante_call: skill > 0 with the 95% bootstrap interval excluding 0
scoring: Report the point estimate, the 95% percentile interval, and the fraction of draws with skill <= 0. Also report per-measure one-sided Wilcoxon tests on 116 rows each with Holm adjustment. The registered 580-row Wilcoxon is still reported, labelled as anti-conservative.

statement: SUPPLEMENT to the registered 90% intervals, added 2026-10-15 after outside review: the registered county intervals are the wider of the bracket carried through the pattern and the pattern-error band, so they are unconditional on the statewide result and their coverage mostly re-grades the level call. Preferred calibration measure: coverage of the relevelled prediction inside the pattern band alone.
metric: share of Missouri rows whose certified share lies within relevelled prediction +/- 1.645 x 0.147 on the logit scale (0.147 = the backtest pattern RMSE registered in the notebook)
scoring: Below 0.85 means the pattern error was understated; above 0.95 means it was padded. The registered unconditional coverage is still reported next to it, with the statewide landing noted.
